sources.evidence: SIMULATION + CALCULATION (Rev H active nose, model H1; nothing measured)
sources.q_lim/q_stop: PROPOSED; SIM: never at its limit with perfect knowledge of 2 mm tremor except peaks at 10-12 Hz (see sweep)
sources.m_tip: CALC (parts in opt/inertial/revh.nose_parts: Ti carrier, D1 refill, Al arm, 4 NdFeB magnets)
sources.F_peak/F_cont: CALC (adjoint design model opt/inertial/adjoint.py; magnet and copper data MFR AMF-28/AMF-29; leakage, fill and end-turn factors ASSUMPTION); peak = Km sqrt(3.7 V x 1.5 A), continuous = Km sqrt(0.35 W) per axis (ASSUMPTION thermal)
sources.servo: ASSUMPTION (modelled in H1 as the stage's 2nd-order follower); sensitivity in the sweep
sources.latency: ASSUMPTION built on MFR OPT-37 (fusion) and CALC for the 2nd-order servo
sources.architecture: B = a skid ring on the FIXED front sleeve carries the writing force; the refill carrier (the moving nose) tilts on a 2-axis flexure gimbal so the ball moves up to +/-3 mm; the refill slides axially on a soft constant-force spring so the ball stays on the paper. Chosen over A (rigid nose carrying the load) by simulation: A's ceiling with perfect knowledge is 0.15-0.77 of the ink error against 0.09-0.24 for B, A needs 0.41 W of copper loss with a bias spring (1.9 W without) against about 0.004 W for B, and a rigid nose must press the tip into the paper for tilt-plane corrections (0.38 N rms writing-force change).
